title: Comparing Software Developers with ChatGPT: An Empirical Investigation
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether ChatGPT can match or outperform human software developers on coding tasks, with a specific focus on objective technical outcomes such as runtime performance and memory efficiency. The authors position the study within broader debates about AI-assisted software engineering and argue that empirical comparisons with human solutions are needed to understand when automated code generation is useful.

The intervention studied is ChatGPT-4 used to generate solutions for LeetCode programming problems. The authors selected one recent LeetCode contest containing four problems of varying difficulty, prompted ChatGPT with the original problem statements, and then submitted the generated code to LeetCode to obtain runtime and memory metrics. They compared these results against solutions previously submitted by 42 human programmers, split into experienced contest programmers and novice/non-contest programmers based on contest rank and participation history.

The study found mixed results. ChatGPT outperformed novice programmers on performance for easy and medium problems, and showed better memory efficiency on one medium problem. However, it did not outperform experienced contest programmers on performance, and it did not consistently beat them on memory efficiency. The authors conclude that AI and human programmers have complementary strengths, and that task allocation in software engineering should depend on developer expertise and task requirements.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-based conversational AI system for generating and evaluating text and code from natural language prompts.
identified_tools.use_case: Used to generate code solutions for LeetCode coding problems and to compare those outputs against solutions produced by human programmers.

findings.finding_summary: In a controlled experiment, ChatGPT-4-generated code was compared with solutions from experienced contest programmers and novice/non-contest programmers on LeetCode problems. The paper reports that ChatGPT outperformed novice programmers on easy and medium problems for performance, and outperformed both experienced and novice programmers on memory efficiency for one medium problem, but did not outperform experienced programmers on performance and did not show superior memory efficiency on easy or hard problems.
findings.measure: LeetCode runtime performance and memory usage / memory efficiency for coding solutions
findings.sample_size: n=42 programmers; ChatGPT outputs for 4 contest problems

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical controlled experiment with explicit comparator groups and quantitative metrics, but it is not a randomized K-12 education study and the paper’s methodology is specific to software engineering rather than classroom instruction. The evidence is internally structured and comparative, but generalizability to education is limited.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effects are task-specific and mixed, with some comparative advantages and some null results, and no standardized effect sizes are reported. Overall impact is unclear to modest rather than clearly medium or large.
